subject.title: Support session-level environment variables for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose per-spawn ACP environment variables through the model-callable `sessions_spawn` tool, or keep credential env injection on an operator-controlled surface such as configured agent env or trusted gateway/API input?
rationale: This changes how credentials reach subprocesses and may expose secrets through model-visible tool arguments, transcripts, logs, or persisted session metadata unless maintainers choose the trust boundary first.

options.title: Prefer operator-controlled env
options.body: Keep raw credential values out of model-callable `sessions_spawn` and use per-agent config or a trusted non-model-visible gateway/API path for env injection.

options.title: Add guarded `sessions_spawn.env`
options.body: Expose the requested tool parameter only with strict env-name validation, redaction, transcript handling, and clear docs about the secret exposure model.

options.title: Defer to adjacent env work
options.body: Wait for the per-agent env PR and per-call sandbox-env discussion to settle before deciding whether ACP needs a separate session-level API.

recommendation.title: Prefer operator-controlled env
recommendation.body: Keep raw credential values out of model-callable `sessions_spawn` and use per-agent config or a trusted non-model-visible gateway/API path for env injection.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced `sessions_spawn` and is the clearest routing owner for the product/security boundary around a model-callable session-spawn surface.
